description: The figure is a single image of Table I, a literature-survey table rendered rotated 90° (text reading bottom-to-top): "Typical tensile properties reported in the literature for some low-density steels20,26,28,32,58". Ten columns are printed — Steel Type, Nominal Composition (wt.%), Processing Condition, YS (MPa), UTS (MPa), UE (%), TE (%), n, r̄ and Reference. Six data rows list: Ferritic (IF) Fe-6.8Al-0.0035C-0.1Ti, cold rolled and annealed (342 MPa, 465 MPa, 18.5%, 31.1%, n=0.17, r̄=1.37, ref 20); Ferritic (BH) Fe-7Al-0.002C-0.01Ti, annealed and strain aged (420, 460a, -, 32a, ref 28); Austenitic Fe-30.5Mn-8Al-1.2C, solutionized and aged (540, 895, 65, 73.6b, n=0.29b, ref 58); Ferrite-based duplex Fe-5.8Al-3.5Mn-0.35C, annealed and aged (553, 830, 34.7b, 40.0, n=0.27b, ref 32); Austenite-based duplex Fe-26Mn-9.7Al-0.54C, annealed (608, 882, 26.7, 30.3, n=0.23, ref 26); Triplex Fe-5.8Al-3.5Mn-0.35C, annealed and aged (667, 794, -, 34.0, n=0.16b, ref 32). YS spans 342-667 MPa and UTS 460-895 MPa. The footnote defines TE, UE, UTS, YS, n and r̄ and marks a-values as annealed condition and b-values as author-derived. The table illustrates the strength-ductility trade-off across low-density steel classes.

subfigures.description: One table image (rotated 90°), titled 'Table I. Typical tensile properties reported in the literature for some low-density steels', with columns Steel Type, Nominal Composition (wt.%), Processing Condition, YS (MPa), UTS (MPa), UE (%), TE (%), n, r̄, Reference and six steel rows plus a defining footnote.

observations.observation: The table lists six steel types: Ferritic (IF), Ferritic (BH), Austenitic, Ferrite-based duplex, Austenite-based duplex and Triplex.
Ferritic (IF) Fe-6.8Al-0.0035C-0.1Ti, cold rolled and annealed, is reported with YS 342 MPa, UTS 465 MPa, UE 18.5%, TE 31.1%, n = 0.17, r̄ = 1.37 (reference 20).
Ferritic (BH) Fe-7Al-0.002C-0.01Ti, annealed and strain aged, is reported with YS 420 MPa and UTS 460a MPa (a-marks denote annealed condition) and TE 32a %; UE, n and r̄ are given as '-'.
Austenitic Fe-30.5Mn-8Al-1.2C, solutionized and aged, shows the highest printed UTS (895 MPa), UE (65%) and TE (73.6b %) of the table, with YS 540 MPa and n = 0.29b.
Triplex Fe-5.8Al-3.5Mn-0.35C, annealed and aged, shows the highest printed YS (667 MPa) together with the lowest UTS (794 MPa) in the table, TE 34.0% and n = 0.16b.

The Ferrite-based duplex and Triplex rows share the same nominal composition Fe-5.8Al-3.5Mn-0.35C and the same processing description (annealed and aged) but are reported with different properties (YS 553 vs 667 MPa; UTS 830 vs 794 MPa).
The normal anisotropy factor r̄ is populated only for Ferritic (IF) as 1.37; every other row shows '-' for r̄.
Austenite-based duplex Fe-26Mn-9.7Al-0.54C, annealed, is reported with YS 608 MPa, UTS 882 MPa, UE 26.7%, TE 30.3% and n = 0.23.

The table footnote defines TE as total elongation, UE as uniform elongation, UTS as ultimate tensile strength, YS as yield strength, n as the strain hardening exponent for the whole range of plastic strain, and r̄ as normal anisotropy factors.
The footnote states that properties marked with 'a' are for the annealed condition and those marked with 'b' were determined by the current authors from data provided in the corresponding references.

The title caption asserts the compilation represents typical tensile properties of some low-density steels taken from the literature, with reference numbers 20, 26, 28, 32 and 58 listed in the header.
Yield strength ranges from 342 MPa (Ferritic IF) to 667 MPa (Triplex) and UTS ranges from 460 MPa (Ferritic BH) to 895 MPa (Austenitic); the highest-strength row is not the most ductile one.
